clue.text: Financial office compassionate about the French royal family?

indicators.note: the word for compassionate goes round the French article, surrounding it

parts.note: caring means kind and compassionate
le is French for 'the'
a royal dynasty is a house, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: A sympathetic bank office takes a kindly view of the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'royal family' is a dynasty's name, House, not a description of the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearing house is a financial institution that settles transactions between banks or traders.

clue.text: Stylish steamship in ceramic material

indicators.note: the steamship abbreviation goes inside the material word

parts.note: pottery is made from clay

explanation.surface: A smart steamship with fine pottery aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Classy means elegant and fashionable, showing good taste.

clue.text: Seaside walk pleased an eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An oddball out strolling along the seafront is delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: An esplanade is a promenade, a paved walkway along a seafront.

clue.text: Bring new supplies of regularly ordered crack

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the next word

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of this word are the ones kept
a crack is a joke or quip

explanation.surface: A wisecrack about stocking up on an order.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth and sixth letters of 'ordered' are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-equip is to provide fresh equipment or stores to replace the old.

clue.text: Return to status quo with two girls at island working

parts.note: the two women's names Norma and Liz
taken as written
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: Two women go to work on an island, getting life back to normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Normalization is the process of restoring things to the usual state or standard.

clue.text: One dislikes headgear carried by old queen

indicators.note: in a down clue the hat sits on top, carried by the queen's letters below it

parts.note: a hat is headgear
ER is Elizabeth Regina, used for an earlier queen

explanation.surface: Someone resents the hat a former queen is wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hater is a person who loathes or detests things, someone who dislikes.

clue.text: What's regularly placed in current container

indicators.note: regularly means picking letters at an even spacing, here the even-numbered ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of this word are the ones kept

explanation.surface: Asks what is routinely placed inside a modern container.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth and sixth letters of 'current' are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or vessel, such as one holding ashes or tea.

clue.text: Opening of organ permitted

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: An organ was allowed an opening, as for surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole for a lace or cord, a little opening.

clue.text: Enough to taste without needing seconds

indicators.note: the abbreviation for seconds is not wanted, so it is dropped from the tasting word

parts.note: to sample food is to taste it

explanation.surface: A diner has had enough from one taste and won't want a second helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' looks like extra helpings at dinner, but it is just S, the abbreviation for seconds of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, more than sufficient for what is needed.

clue.text: Regret holding English twit back in train

indicators.note: the regret word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: back means the word for twit is read in reverse

parts.note: a nit (nitwit) is a foolish person

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having an English fool on board a train with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' here is not the railway but the group of attendants following an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the body of followers or attendants accompanying a dignitary, like a bride's train.

clue.text: Casual pressure breaking shoulder-bone

indicators.note: breaking up the letters of casual and the pressure abbreviation lets them be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Light, casual pressure is enough to break someone's shoulder blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The scapula is the anatomical name for the shoulder blade.

clue.text: Bond again exposing some backward counterfeiters

indicators.note: backward tells us the concealed run reads right to left
only some letters of the final word are revealed, the run lying inside it

parts.note: the letters run inside this word, then turned round

explanation.surface: Captured forgers are tied up once more after being exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie is to fasten or knot something a second time, binding it once more.

clue.text: Consequently European umpire gets involved in other foul

indicators.note: the umpire and European pieces become caught up inside the jumbled letters
foul means messed up, so the letters of other are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
ref is short for referee, an umpire

explanation.surface: A European referee ends up embroiled in someone else's foul, as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore means for that reason, as a result.

clue.text: Copy round short piece of advice for new staff member

indicators.note: the copying word goes round the shortened advice word

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a pointer is a helpful hint or tip

explanation.surface: A tip for a new recruit: copy someone, after a brief word of advice.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointee is a person who has just been given a job or post.

clue.text: Suit man working for a big rise in the main

definitions.text: a big rise in the main

indicators.note: working the letters over means rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A businessman in a suit works hard to bring about a big rise in income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic name for the open sea, so the big rise is a wave, not a pay increase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave, a massive surge of ocean water.

clue.text: Store energy transformed as a type of sound

indicators.note: the store letters plus the energy abbreviation are changed in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stored energy is converted into sound, like a battery feeding a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Stereo is sound reproduced through two channels, giving a spatial effect.

clue.text: Young bird making noise like a small seal

indicators.note: the answer sounds like the word for a small seal

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: A baby bird is barking like a little seal pup.
explanation.walkthrough: The seal is not the animal but a stamp used to mark wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan.

clue.text: Don't start to strain lock

indicators.note: an instruction not to begin means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: stress is strain or tension

explanation.surface: An instruction not to force a stiff lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of a person's hair.

clue.text: Mostly remain around old Greek philosopher

indicators.note: the shortened remaining word goes around the old abbreviation
mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: to stick is to remain or stay put

explanation.surface: Most stay around the ancient Greek thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic is a follower of the Greek school of philosophy founded by Zeno.

clue.text: Deeply carved in a cathedral

parts.note: taken as written
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
cut means carved

explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small English city famous for its cathedral; crosswords often use it this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acutely means intensely or keenly, as in feeling something deeply.

clue.text: Runs an old instrument, one making pasta

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
taken as written
the viol is an early stringed instrument
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A musician runs an antique instrument while also cooking pasta.

clue.text: Compete with four in Germany, right away

indicators.note: the right abbreviation is sent away from the German word

parts.note: vier is German for four

clue.text: Navy going after a company as a source of oak

indicators.note: the navy abbreviation comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The navy follows a company in pursuit of good timber for shipbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak tree grows from an acorn, its seed-bearing nut.

clue.text: Excessively bold oddball I've confronted

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of facing up to a strange character, a little too boldly.
